title: Plant Buddy
intro: Check if a plant needs water. Show a happy or thirsty face on the screen.

steps.title: Read the soil
steps.text:
The soil sensor's two prongs measure how easily electricity flows through the soil. Water helps electricity flow, so wet and dry soil give different numbers.

**Your task:** Run the code and open the **Serial Monitor**. Hold the sensor in the air, then dip the prongs in a glass of water. Write down both numbers: you'll need them! (In the simulator, use the slider.)
hints: Only dip the prongs, not the electronics at the top.
Dry gives one number, wet gives a different one. Which is bigger?
Most sensors give a bigger number when dry.

checks.label: I wrote down my dry and wet numbers

steps.success: Your board can feel the soil. Those two numbers let you turn readings into a percentage.

steps.title: Test the screen and LED
steps.text:
Before joining everything up, check the screen and the LED on their own. The screen shows a message and the LED lights up.

**Your task:** fill in the blank so the LED turns on, then Run.

checks.label: I can see the message and the LED

steps.success: Screen and LED both work. Now let's join them to the soil sensor.

steps.title: Plant buddy
steps.text:
**Goal:** the screen shows how wet the soil is as a percentage (dry = 0 %, wet = 100 %), and says "Water me!" with the LED on when it's under 30 %. Otherwise it says "Happy :)".

The starter code has the screen set up. Use your dry and wet numbers from the last step.
hints: `map(soil, DRY, WET, 0, 100)` turns DRY into 0 and WET into 100. `constrain` keeps it between 0 and 100.
Use `if (wetness < 30)` to choose the message, and turn the LED on or off too.
Use **Watch the goal** to see one way to do it.

checks.label: It asks for water when dry
It says "Water me!" when the sensor is dry

steps.success: Your plant has a buddy! Turning a raw reading into a percentage is called calibration.

outro: Your plant buddy looks after a plant: it reads the soil, turns the reading into a percentage, and tells you when to water. Real smart gardens work the same way.
stretch: Show a happy or sad face on the screen, drawn with circles and lines.
Only water warnings in the daytime: add a light sensor and stay quiet at night.
Remember the driest reading of the day and show it.
